cognate: ON garðr ~ Ved. gṛhá- (*gʰordʰ-/*gʰr̥dʰ- 'enclosure, house'); faðir ~ pitṛ́-, móðir ~ mātṛ́-, bróðir ~ bhrā́tṛ- (all four members cognate)
drift_or_renewal: garðr 'enclosure, farmstead' vs gṛhá 'house' (minor semantic shift); ON adds the daughter's seduction, AV the binding spell
shared_syntax: kin-term genitive(s) governing a locative/dative of the 'house/garth' noun; the same triad father/mother/brother coordinated (ON 'faður garðe eða moðor eða broðor', AV 'mātuḥ ... gṛhe atha u bhrātuḥ atha u pituḥ')
context: Both are about an unmarried daughter whose status is fixed by her residence in the house of her natal kin: the Norwegian law (Gulathing inheritance chapter, several MSS) settles the inheritance of a daughter seduced 'in the garth of father, mother or brother'; AV 1.14 (= AVP 1.15) binds a maiden (kanyā) to stay in the house of mother, brother and father as an old maid (kulapā). The Sanskrit epic uses 'pitur gṛhe' formulaically of daughters (Ambā, Damayantī).
phrase: *ph₂tros gʰordʰ- 'in the father's (mother's, brother's) enclosure' of an unmarried daughter

near_miss.why_not: sun/darkness collocation is generic natural description; ON is an eclipse miracle at Stiklestad, Vuk a formulaic nightfall; cognates sól~sunce, myrkr~mrak are everyday words

near_miss.why_not: kin-term enumerations are universal; no shared verb or figure beyond the list itself (ON drepa vs Skt han not cognate)

near_miss.lead: father/mother/brother/sister enumeration in inheritance and guardianship law ~ Vedic/epic kin lists
near_miss.why_not: generic kin enumeration; contexts not congruent (inheritance order vs fever charm/epic catalogue)
